reasoning_steps: The current throughput of 17.67 Mbps is significantly below the target of 50 Mbps, necessitating a more aggressive growth strategy.
The average RTT of 159.82 ms is well above the 20 ms target, suggesting a high-latency network path where bufferbloat must be minimized.
BBR1 is currently failing to reach the throughput target, likely due to a conservative estimate of the bandwidth-delay product in this specific environment.
The new algorithm will implement a hybrid delay-based and loss-based approach to balance throughput and latency goals.
In the congestion avoidance phase, the window will scale proportionally to the difference between the current RTT and the minimum observed RTT.
A target CWND of approximately 666 packets is calculated to achieve 50 Mbps at a 160 ms RTT, which the algorithm will aim for.
The 'llm_ssthresh' function is designed to reduce the window to half of the flight size upon congestion to maintain stability.
The 'llm_undo_cwnd' function is implemented to allow the window to recover quickly if a packet loss is determined to be spurious.
